Package io.webagent4j.workflow

Record Class WorkflowIntrospectionReport

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.webagent4j.workflow.WorkflowIntrospectionReport
Record Components:
workflowId - the inspected definition's identifier
definitionNodeCount - the total number of IWorkflowSteps present in the definition, counted once each at every nesting depth (a loop body's steps, a conditional branch's steps, and a parallel branch's steps are each counted exactly once, structurally - never unrolled or multiplied by any declared bound)
maximumControlFlowDepth - the deepest combined WorkflowStepType.CONDITIONAL/WorkflowStepType.LOOP/WorkflowStepType.PARALLEL nesting level this definition actually reaches - the exact same counter and semantics as Workflow#MAX_CONTROL_FLOW_NESTING_DEPTH enforces at Workflow.Builder#build() time, never a second, divergent definition; always at most that bound, since this report can only be produced for an already-built, already-valid Workflow
conditionalCount - the number of WorkflowStepType.CONDITIONAL steps, at any depth
loopCount - the number of WorkflowStepType.LOOP steps, at any depth
parallelCount - the number of WorkflowStepType.PARALLEL steps, at any depth
actionCount - the number of WorkflowStepType.ACTION steps, at any depth
declaredInputCount - requiredInputCount + optionalInputCount
requiredInputCount - the number of declared required inputs
optionalInputCount - the number of declared optional inputs
inputs - every declared input's own metadata, in declaration order (required inputs, then optional inputs) - never a value
declaredOutputCount - the number of distinct output variables declared by some step, at any depth (a variable published identically by more than one structurally exclusive branch is still counted once, since it is one logical variable - see WorkflowVariable.equals(java.lang.Object))
definitelyAvailableOutputCount - the number of declared outputs that are definitely available - see WorkflowIntrospectionOutput.definitelyAvailable()
secretOutputCount - the number of declared outputs that are WorkflowVariable.secret()
outputs - every declared output's own metadata, in definition-traversal order - never a value
maximumLoopIterations - the largest maxIterations declared by any single WorkflowStepType.LOOP step in this definition, or 0 if loopCount() is zero - never a sum or product across multiple loops, which maximumPotentialExecutionNodes() already accounts for
maximumParallelBranches - the largest branch count declared by any single WorkflowStepType.PARALLEL step in this definition, or 0 if parallelCount() is zero
totalParallelBranches - the sum, across every WorkflowStepType.PARALLEL step in this definition, of that step's own declared branch count - a purely structural definition-count, never multiplied by any enclosing loop's maxIterations
maximumPotentialExecutionNodes - a conservative upper bound on the number of entries WorkflowResult#steps() could contain for any single valid execution of this workflow, given its declared structural bounds (maxIterations for every loop, the declared branch count for every parallel step, and the more expensive of a conditional's two branches) - see docs/workflow.md#static-workflow-introspection for the exact formula and why it is a worst case, never a prediction. Saturates at Long.MAX_VALUE rather than silently overflowing - see maximumPotentialExecutionNodesSaturated()
maximumPotentialExecutionNodesSaturated - whether maximumPotentialExecutionNodes() reached Long.MAX_VALUE because the true worst-case count overflowed a long, rather than because the true worst case happens to equal Long.MAX_VALUE exactly - a caller that needs to tell these two cases apart must check this flag, never compare the count itself to Long.MAX_VALUE
mayExceedRuntimeNodeBudget - whether maximumPotentialExecutionNodes() exceeds this engine's own cumulative executed-step-node budget, or whether that computation saturated before a definitive comparison could be made - see docs/workflow.md#static-workflow-introspection. This is information for a caller's own policy, never a validation failure: true does not mean this workflow is invalid or will fail, only that its declared structural bounds do not rule out eventually reaching that budget
containsActions - whether actionCount() is greater than zero
containsLoops - whether loopCount() is greater than zero
containsParallelism - whether parallelCount() is greater than zero
containsSecrets - whether this definition declares at least one secret input or output
riskIndicators - every WorkflowStaticRiskIndicator that applies to this definition, at most one instance of each, always in WorkflowStaticRiskIndicator's own declaration order - never a score, never caller-influenced ordering
public record WorkflowIntrospectionReport(WorkflowId workflowId, long definitionNodeCount, int maximumControlFlowDepth, long conditionalCount, long loopCount, long parallelCount, long actionCount, int declaredInputCount, int requiredInputCount, int optionalInputCount, List<WorkflowIntrospectionInput> inputs, int declaredOutputCount, int definitelyAvailableOutputCount, int secretOutputCount, List<WorkflowIntrospectionOutput> outputs, int maximumLoopIterations, int maximumParallelBranches, long totalParallelBranches, long maximumPotentialExecutionNodes, boolean maximumPotentialExecutionNodesSaturated, boolean mayExceedRuntimeNodeBudget, boolean containsActions, boolean containsLoops, boolean containsParallelism, boolean containsSecrets, List<WorkflowStaticRiskIndicator> riskIndicators) extends Record
Immutable, deterministic, backend-neutral static-complexity and safety-surface summary of a Workflow definition, produced by WorkflowIntrospector.inspect(Workflow) without ever executing anything - see docs/workflow.md#static-workflow-introspection.

This is a structural sibling to WorkflowValidationReport, WorkflowExecutionPlan, and WorkflowExecutionTree, not a replacement for any of them:

  • WorkflowValidationReport answers is this definition structurally coherent, and why (or why not)?
  • WorkflowExecutionPlan answers what could structurally execute?
  • This report answers how complex is that structure, and what bounded runtime pressure may it represent?
  • WorkflowExecutionTree answers what actually executed?

Secret safety: this report is safe to log. It contains metadata only - names, declared runtime types, counts, and booleans - and never a workflow input or output value, secret or otherwise.

No score: every field here is a measurable, individually documented fact. There is no combined "risk score" or "complexity score" - see riskIndicators() for the closest thing, a small set of named structural facts a caller's own policy may act on.

Upper bounds, not predictions: maximumPotentialExecutionNodes() and every field derived from it describe what this workflow's declared structural bounds permit in the worst case - never a prediction of what a particular execution will actually do. A condition is never evaluated to compute this report, so a loop that always exits after its first iteration in practice is indistinguishable, here, from one that always runs to its declared maxIterations bound; both report the same worst-case potential. See docs/workflow.md#static-workflow-introspection for the complete list of limitations.
